title: Sra's Six-Matrix Trace Inequality — Lean-Checked Counterexample
description: An explicit rational counterexample, checked in Lean with standard axioms, to Δ₆ > 0 for Sra's alternating sum of inverses of sums of six positive definite matrices (MathOverflow 263833).
summary: Six explicit rational 3×3 positive definite matrices give Δ₆ ≈ −99.97 < 0, so the six-matrix trace consequence of Sra's quantum coupon collector conjecture fails. The underlying conjecture was already refuted by Sra, and this failure follows from his Theorem 8.4 by a short argument.

problem.name: Six-matrix trace consequence of Sra's quantum coupon collector conjecture (Δ₆ > 0)

problem.sourceHtml: Suvrit Sra, MathOverflow question 263833 (2017), reproduced as Problem 8.1 of S. Sra, GPT, the Counterexample Machine, arXiv:2608.29595 (2026). The trace quantity Δn and the remark that its sign is undecided for 6 ≤ n ≤ 9 are in Appendix E of that paper.

verification.summary: Lean 4.35.0 with Mathlib v4.35.0; all 18 audited declarations depend only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound, and the proof is replayed by Lean's kernel checker and the independent nanoda checker.

priority.statement: An independently constructed counterexample. Sra refuted the underlying conjecture (arXiv:2608.29595, Theorem 8.4). His paper lists this six-matrix trace form as undecided, but its failure follows from Theorem 8.4 by a short congruence argument, given below. No novelty or priority is claimed.

earlier.label: S. Sra, arXiv:2608.29595, Theorem 8.4: six 3×3 matrices with a negative quadratic form of Q₆ (refutes the six-matrix Loewner-order statement)
S. Sra, arXiv:2608.29595, Appendix E: ten matrices with Δ₁₀ < 0 (the trace form for n = 10)

claimHtml:
For real symmetric positive definite d×d matrices X1, …, Xn, write XS = Σi∈S Xi and

Qn = Σk=1n (−1)k+1 Σ|S|=k XS−1,    Δn = tr Qn = Σ∅≠S⊆[n] (−1)|S|−1 tr XS−1.

Sra's question (MathOverflow 263833; Problem 8.1 of arXiv:2608.29595) asks whether Qn ≻ 0. Positive definiteness implies Δn > 0. The paper proves Δn > 0 for n ≤ 5, gives a counterexample at n = 10, and lists the trace form as undecided for 6 ≤ n ≤ 9. The claim refuted here is the n = 6 trace form: Δ6 > 0 for every dimension d ≥ 1 and all six real symmetric positive definite Xi.
counterexampleHtml:
Let E = diag(1/100, 1, 1) and, for t ∈ {−3, −2, −1, 1, 2, 3}, vt = (t², 200, 200t)T and Xt = E + vtvtT. These are six rational 3×3 symmetric positive definite matrices, and

−99.97093178 < Δ6(X−3, …, X3) < −99.97093177.

The exact value is a rational number with a 376-digit numerator and a 374-digit denominator, stated in the Lean source.
explanationHtml: Each Xt is the sum of a positive definite diagonal matrix and a positive semidefinite rank-one matrix, so it is positive definite, and every subset sum XS is invertible. Evaluating all 63 nonempty-subset terms exactly gives Δ6 < 0, contradicting Δ6 > 0 (and also Δ6 ≥ 0). Since a positive semidefinite matrix has nonnegative trace, the same tuple also shows Q6 is not positive semidefinite; that Loewner-order failure was already established by Sra's Theorem 8.4.
verificationHtml:
Formalized in Lean 4.35.0 with Mathlib v4.35.0 using Mathlib's own Matrix, Matrix.PosDef, Matrix.trace, and matrix inverse. The main theorem is SraSixMatrix.six_matrix_trace_positivity_false : ¬ SixMatrixTracePositivity; trace_Q proves Δn = tr Qn for all n and d, and Verification.lean restates the claim using Mathlib definitions only. The exact value is computed by a proved trace-of-inverse formula for 3×3 matrices and norm_num.

Trust model: Lean's kernel and the standard axioms propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound, for all 18 audited declarations. The sources contain no sorry, admit, custom axiom, decide, or native_decide. The exported proof is re-checked from an empty environment by Lean's kernel checker and by nanoda, an independent type checker. A separate Python verifier using only exact rational arithmetic recomputes Δ6 by two inversion methods.
priorArtHtml:
• Sra's Theorem 8.4 (arXiv:2608.29595) gives six rational 3×3 matrices with −96 < vTQ6v < −95, refuting the six-matrix Loewner-order statement. Appendix E gives ten matrices with Δ10 < 0.
  • The six-matrix trace failure follows from Theorem 8.4 by an elementary common-congruence argument: if vTQ6(X)v < 0, then Yi = CXiCT for a suitable invertible C gives tr Q6(Y) < 0. Concretely, tr Q6(Y) = tr(Q6(X)W) with W = C−1C−T, and W = vvT + εI makes it negative. The paper does not state this deduction, and its Appendix E lists 6 ≤ n ≤ 9 as undecided for the trace form; the deduction was made in a prior-art audit for this work on October 16, 2026.
  • The witness here differs from both published tuples. Its only advantages are a compact parameterization and a machine-checked exact value; no minimality is claimed.
provenanceHtml: Chris Ozols, with AI-assisted development and formalization. The counterexample was found during an AI-assisted investigation in October 2026 and first checked by exact rational arithmetic. A prior-art audit on October 16, 2026 concluded that the six-matrix trace failure is a routine consequence of Sra's Theorem 8.4. The Lean formalization, the independent Python verifier, and the repository were produced with Anthropic's Claude on October 27, 2026.
